subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw fold these anti-drift guards into the broader structured run lifecycle contract, or implement them as a separate enforcement layer?
rationale: The requested behavior changes public run/status semantics, persisted state ownership, telemetry, and config surface; automation cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Unify With Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Define begin/progress-evidence/escalation/commit-or-abort once and use this issue as the guardrail portion of the structured lifecycle work.

options.title: Implement Narrow Guard Layer
options.body: Add per-run guard state and timers behind an explicit flag while preserving the existing public lifecycle event shape for now.

options.title: Keep Only Tool-Loop Guards
options.body: Treat current tool-loop detection and narrower sibling issues as sufficient, then close or narrow this item to documentation and tuning.

recommendation.title: Unify With Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Define begin/progress-evidence/escalation/commit-or-abort once and use this issue as the guardrail portion of the structured lifecycle work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway audit/protocol ownership and prior lifecycle review context make steipete the best available routing owner.
